question: Who started the Mahila Seva Mandal to promote women's rights in 1852 ?
solution:
The correct answer is__ **Savitribai Phule.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Savitribai Phule**

 
 
• **​**Savitribai Phule was a **poet, educationalist, and social reformer** from Maharashtra, India.
 
• In Maharashtra, along with her** husband, Mahatma Jyotiba Phule**, she contributed significantly to the advancement of women's rights in India.
 
• She is thought to have started the **feminist movement** in India. In** 1848**, Savitribai and her husband **established Bhide wada**, one of the **first modern Indian girls' schools, in Pune.**
 
• In **1818**, **Robert May of the London Missionary Society **was the first to establish a **school** solely for girls in the **Chinsurah region of Bengal**. She worked to eliminate** caste and gender-based discrimination** and unfair treatment.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ramabai Ranade**

 
 
• **​**Indian social worker Ramabai Ranade was born on 25 January 1862 and died on 25 January 1924. She was one of the **first advocates for women's rights** in the early 20th century.
 
 
 
• ​**Annie Besant**
 
 
• **​**Annie Besant was a **British socialist, theosophist, freemason, activist for women's rights** and Home Rule, educator, and advocate for Indian nationalism. She was born on October 1, 1847, and died on September 20, 1933.
